x: Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth. Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner.
Although we had four representatives in the mile they had to fill the last four places behind P.Driver(4m.19.8s.), E.Earl (4.23.1), J.Edgar and C.Wilson.
"Jumbo" was first past the cameras but 21st across the finishing line. Twenty of the reasons for this can be seen close behind and include P.

Schools mile in the third fastest ever time of 4:28.2 (remember this was 15 years ago) following this up with 2nd in the All-England Schools and a win over Peter Driver in the Surrey Junior mile in a record 4:25.6.

Jimmy Green of ATHLETICS WEEKLY wrote afterwards "Much depended on the ability of the early South London runners to keep in touch with the leaders, so that Gordon Pirie and Peter Driver could put them in a winning position on stages 7 and 8.

He won the LAC Schools mile in the third fastest ever time of 4:28.2 (something special in those days), finished 2nd in the All-England Schools and beat Peter Driver in the Surrey Junior Mile with a record 4:25.6.
Peter Driver was Foster's unofficial representative at one time. Foster did a mail-order service to foot outlines and I well remember giving him my own specification for a thick sandwich sole.
